NEVER write prices here — every price on the page is generated from tools.json via the engine. This file holds prose only: intro tagline, a warning box, 'when worth it' rows, FAQ (questions + price-free answers), and CTA cross-links. Questions whose answer needs a live price are generated by the module, not stored here.

conventions.intro: lead paragraph under the h1 (no price)
conventions.warn: optional amber warning box — HTML allowed, no hardcoded price (the module appends the real at-volume figure where useful)
conventions.whenWorthIt: list of {case, verdict, tier} rows; tier = good|warn|bad → coloured cell
conventions.faq: list of {q, a} — a is HTML, NO prices; price-bearing FAQ rows are appended by the module

zapier.h1: Zapier Pricing 2026 — Is It Worth It?
zapier.intro: Zapier is the most widely known automation tool — and the most expensive. Here's what you actually pay per month, and what cheaper alternatives exist for the same workflows.
zapier.warn: Zapier prices by task tier, and the per-run cost stays steep as you scale — far above the volume pricing of Make or self-hosted tools. Check your run tier before committing to an annual plan.

whenWorthIt.case: Need a very specific app integration not offered by other tools
Non-technical user who wants the simplest possible UI
Very low volume (under the free tier)
Higher volume and comfortable with a learning curve
whenWorthIt.verdict: Switch to Make — far cheaper per run

whenWorthIt.case: Developer, comfortable self-hosting
Need GDPR / EU data residency

faq.q: Does Zapier charge per task or per Zap?
faq.a: Zapier charges per task (each action-step execution), not per Zap. A 3-step Zap that runs 100 times costs 300 tasks (the trigger doesn't count). On this site we normalise that to runs × steps so you can compare it like-for-like with other tools — which is why a multi-step Zap gets expensive fast.

faq.q: Can I use Zapier for free?
faq.a: Yes, but Zapier's free plan is very limited and adds a polling delay. Make's free plan is significantly more generous on included runs and scenarios.

make.h1: Make (Integromat) Pricing 2026 — Plans & Real Cost per Run
make.intro: Make is the volume-pricing favourite — the same cloud experience as Zapier at a fraction of the per-run cost. Here's what each plan really costs as your run count grows.
make.warn: Make meters credits (formerly "operations"): one module action = one credit, code execution counts double. The headline plan price covers a fixed credit pool — overshoot it and you move up a tier, so size your plan to your real run volume.

whenWorthIt.case: Want cloud convenience without Zapier's price
High run volume on a budget
Comfortable with a visual scenario builder
Need an integration Make doesn't have
Want to eliminate the monthly bill entirely
Need strict EU data residency on managed hosting

faq.q: What is an operation (credit) on Make?
faq.a: Each module action in a scenario consumes one credit; code-execution steps count double. We express this as runs × steps so a 3-step scenario that fires 1,000 times is comparable across every tool on this site.
For the same workflow volume, Make is typically several times cheaper per run because it prices by credit pool rather than per task. See the comparison table above for the gap at your volume.

n8n.h1: n8n Pricing 2026 — Cloud vs Self-Hosted Cost
n8n.intro: n8n is the source-available automation tool developers reach for. You can pay for managed Cloud, run it on a cheap VPS, or host it on your own hardware for the price of the electricity. Here's the real cost of each path.
n8n.warn: n8n's self-hosted edition is free, source-available software (Sustainable Use License) — the figures below for VPS and own-server are infrastructure cost (server, database, electricity), not a licence fee. They assume light workflows and exclude your own time to run it.

whenWorthIt.case: Developer comfortable with a server
Want managed hosting, no DevOps
Need GDPR / EU data residency
Non-technical and want a no-code UI
Need a huge third-party app catalog
No appetite for any infrastructure

faq.q: Is n8n really free if I self-host?
faq.a: The software is free under n8n's Sustainable Use licence. You still pay for somewhere to run it — a small VPS, or your own hardware plus electricity. Both are far below cloud-tool pricing, which is why self-hosting wins on cost at scale.

faq.q: What's the difference between VPS and own-server self-hosting?
faq.a: VPS means renting a small cloud server billed monthly. Own-server means running n8n on hardware you already own (a mini PC or Raspberry Pi) — the only recurring cost is electricity, with a one-off hardware outlay shown separately below.

pipedream.h1: Pipedream Pricing 2026 — Credits & Real Cost per Run
pipedream.intro: Pipedream is the developer-first automation platform that prices on compute credits. Here's what each plan costs as your run volume climbs, and where it lands against the alternatives.
pipedream.warn: Pipedream meters credits per workflow execution, and the public per-credit overage rate has been pulled from the pricing page — high-volume overage is now a sales conversation. The Business tier carries the over-volume estimate. Size your plan carefully.

whenWorthIt.case: Developer who lives in code steps
Event-driven, low-to-mid volume
Want a generous component / API catalog
Very high volume
Non-technical, want a visual builder
Need to eliminate the monthly bill

faq.q: How does Pipedream's credit pricing work?
faq.a: Each workflow execution consumes credits based on compute time; paid plans include a monthly credit pool. We normalise this to runs × steps so it lines up with the other tools in the table above.
It's developer-first — the real power is in code steps and APIs. If you want a drag-and-drop no-code builder, Make or Activepieces will feel friendlier.

activepieces.h1: Activepieces Pricing 2026 — Cloud vs Self-Hosted Cost
activepieces.intro: Activepieces is the MIT-licensed (open-core) automation tool with a Zapier-like no-code UI. You can use managed Cloud, run it on a VPS, or self-host on your own hardware. Here's the real cost of each path.
activepieces.warn: Activepieces' self-hosted core is MIT-licensed (open-core) — the self-hosted figures below are infrastructure cost (server / electricity), not a licence fee. Cloud is priced per active flow rather than per run, so flow count drives the bill.

whenWorthIt.case: Want a no-code UI you can also self-host
Care about a truly permissive (MIT) licence
Developer who wants near-free at scale
Need code steps
Need a large third-party app catalog
Run a very large number of active flows on Cloud

faq.a: The software is MIT-licensed and free to self-host. On Cloud you pay per active flow above the free allowance. Self-hosting on a VPS or your own hardware costs only infrastructure, shown below.

faq.q: How is Activepieces priced — per run or per flow?
faq.a: Cloud bills per active flow, not per run, so heavy-volume workflows don't inflate the price the way per-task tools do. We still show a normalised runs cost in the table above for a like-for-like comparison.

automatisch.intro: Automatisch is a simple, EU-friendly open-source automation tool. There's no general cloud plan any more — you run it on a VPS or your own hardware. Here's the real infrastructure cost of each path.
automatisch.warn: Automatisch's managed cloud was discontinued; the realistic options are self-host on a VPS or on your own server. The figures below are infrastructure cost (server / electricity), not a licence fee — it's AGPL-3.0 open-source software.

whenWorthIt.case: Want a simple, EU-friendly open-source tool
Care about GDPR / data sovereignty
Comfortable running a small server
Need a large integration catalog
Need multi-user or API access
Want managed hosting with no DevOps
whenWorthIt.verdict: No general cloud — pick n8n Cloud

faq.q: Does Automatisch have a cloud plan?
faq.a: Not a general one any more — managed hosting was discontinued, so the practical choices are self-hosting on a rented VPS or on your own hardware. Both costs are shown above.
Yes — it's AGPL-3.0 open-source software. You only pay for infrastructure to run it, which at low volume is a few dollars a month.

node-red.intro: Node-RED is the free, flow-based programming tool for wiring together devices, APIs and services. It's self-hosted by design — on a VPS or your own hardware. Here's the real infrastructure cost.
node-red.warn: Node-RED is free Apache-2.0 software with no cloud tier of its own; the figures below are infrastructure cost (server / electricity), not a licence fee. It shines for IoT and event wiring, less so for big SaaS-integration catalogs.

whenWorthIt.case: IoT / hardware / event wiring
Want a free tool on your own hardware
Developer comfortable with flows and JS
Need polished SaaS integrations
Non-technical, want a hosted no-code UI
Need built-in multi-user / team admin

faq.a: The software is free and open-source (Apache-2.0). The only cost is the infrastructure to run it — a small VPS, or your own hardware plus electricity, both shown above.
Partly. It excels at IoT, device and API wiring, but it has no large prebuilt SaaS-integration catalog. For business-app automation, Make, Zapier or n8n are usually a better fit.
